scope: Hook process wall time through the native adapter against a running daemon, scripts/benchmark_hooks.py --provider claude --shell direct --samples 20 --idle-seconds 3 --event <event> --adapter-executable native/target/release/agent-watchdog-hook.exe. Stop is never subscribed (the zero path: one bounded read of policy/socket.json). PostToolUse (all tools) and PreToolUse (a Bash call) are subscribed by the built-in rules, so each call makes a loopback round trip to the daemon and no rule matches (the command differs per call). Two rounds per event, run in the order Stop, PostToolUse, PreToolUse within a round.
note: The host was busier than during the WD-140 A/B (the unsubscribed Stop path had a 35.6 ms sequential p50 then and 49-59 ms now), so absolute figures are higher than WD-140's and only the comparison inside this file is meaningful. Every run delivered all 57 events with zero loss counters.

summary.reading: The subscribed paths are not distinguishable from the unsubscribed one inside the host's noise at this sample size (20 sequential and 20 four-way calls per run): sequential p50 and p95 are no higher, and the four-way p95 ranges overlap. This shows the round trip adds no cost larger than the run-to-run variation; it does not bound it below that.

correctness_check: The benchmark only proves the cost of calls no rule matches. That the subscribed path really reaches the daemon and renders an action is covered by tests/test_rust_adapter.py::test_native_asks_before_a_destructive_command_and_lets_others_pass_with_a_real_daemon and ::test_a_running_daemon_picks_up_a_rule_approved_while_it_runs.
